translation: Pallavi (Chorus): Brave youth, brave youth, Venu Gopalu... my million forms, Venu Gopalu... my million forms. Mother writes a letter of hope, sent through the moon — receive it, sons. Venu Gopalu... my million forms. Mother writes a letter of hope, sent through the moon — receive it, sons. Brave youth, brave youth, Venu Gopalu... my million forms.

Verse 1: In the nest of our dreams your father is not here, my child — this sorrowful news the wind has brought you, my child. That day, in battle, who was it that fell? Between you and me a kingdom drew its line... (between you and me a kingdom drew its line) Iron curtains hold back an iron-clad love... (iron curtains hold back an iron-clad love) Receive it, sons, through that same moon — send your reply back through the same moonlight. (Brave youth, brave youth...)

Verse 2: Whatever bamboo becomes a flute, whatever tune it plays, this mother's lullaby is your father's very word. Even if you cross rivers, you cannot cross my heart. Your footsteps are your father's dreams... (your footsteps are your father's dreams) they move on as light and shadow... (they move on as light and shadow). Tell me your address and send a parrot messenger — I will teach it all my words of love and send it back to you. (Brave youth, brave youth...)

Verse 3: Which hill's jasmine became your bride and stood by you? Which raw, unripe fruit filled your stomach? Whose people's kingdom is it, whose republic's kingdom is it? The Dandakaranyam forest, its fiercest hero... (the Dandakaranyam forest, its fiercest hero) are you not Mother India's firstborn child?... (are you not Mother India's firstborn child?) It would be good if this mother's dimming eyes could see that day; it is enough if you live on, drawing from my own lifespan. (Brave youth, brave youth...)

Verse 4: A thousand eyes were not enough to see you in jail; among the people, they became a million gazes. That old brave Telangana, that struggle of Telangana — will it come back again, will it rise up blazing again?... (will it come back again, will it rise up blazing again?) Is it only your restlessness that will win?... (is it only your restlessness that will win?) Every day you go on swimming against the current, while today I remain curled like a dove in this nest. (Brave youth, brave youth...)

Verse 5: I hope you will remain as the light of my eyes; I hope you will listen even to the beat of my heart. This is not just a complaint, it is every mother's last wish. From forest to village, may you become a bridge of rainbows... (from forest to village, may you become a bridge of rainbows) if you come, I will bless you and send you off... (if you come, I will bless you and send you off). Children of my eyes, babies of my lap, receive, my sons, your mother's cool blessings; receive, my sons, your mother's blessings. Your mother's blessings... Madhuramma's blessings. Your mother's blessings... Madhuramma's blessings. Madhuramma's blessings...
summaryEn: "Veera Kishora Veera Kishora" is an elegy in the voice of a grieving mother writing to her son (or sons) who have gone into the forest as fighters in the Telangana armed struggle. Using the recurring images of the moon and a parrot as go-betweens, she addresses her children fighting far away, in what the lyrics directly name as the Dandakaranyam forest. She mourns the absent father, recalls seeing her children in jail, and asks whether the "old brave Telangana" struggle will rise again. The tone moves between tender maternal imagery — a nest, a lullaby, a letter — and larger political mourning for a movement and its fighters, closing with the mother's repeated blessing, tenderly signed "Madhuramma." The source recording credits the singer Vimalakka; within the "Elegy" category, the song reflects a tradition of maternal lament songs tied to the history of the Telangana movement.
summaryTe: ఈ గేయం తెలంగాణ సాయుధ పోరాటంలో అడవుల్లోకి వెళ్లిన తన కొడుకు(ల)ను ఉద్దేశించి ఒక తల్లి రాసిన కరుణ గీతం లాంటిది. చందమామను, రామచిలుకను సందేశహరులుగా వాడుతూ, దండకారణ్యంలో పోరాడుతున్న బిడ్డలను తలుచుకుంటూ తల్లి తన ఆవేదనను వ్యక్తం చేస్తుంది. తండ్రి లేని లోటు, జైలులో బిడ్డలను చూసిన జ్ఞాపకాలు, పాత తెలంగాణ పోరు మళ్లీ రగులుతుందా అని ఆమె ప్రశ్నించడం ఇందులో కనిపిస్తాయి. వ్యక్తిగత మాతృప్రేమను రాజకీయ పోరాట చరిత్రతో పెనవేస్తూ, గూడు, జోలపాట, ఉత్తరం వంటి గృహసంబంధ ప్రతీకలను ఉపయోగిస్తుంది. పాట చివర్లో తల్లి దీవెనలు 'మధురమ్మ దీవెనలు' అనే పల్లవిలా పదేపదే వస్తాయి. మూలం రికార్డింగ్ ప్రకారం ఈ పాట విమలక్కకు ఆపాదించబడింది, ఎలిజీ కోవలో తెలంగాణ ఉద్యమ అమరవీరుల స్మృతిగీతాల సంప్రదాయానికి చెందినది.
